headline: Last session: Surging oil prices and selloff drag Indian equity benchmark indices to weekly losses

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 27 October.

why: Surging crude oil prices weighed heavily on Indian equity benchmark indices.
Banking stocks faced sharp selling pressure, dragging Bank Nifty down nearly 3%.
Geopolitical concerns and global cues added to market volatility during the week.
Investors stayed cautious ahead of Q2 corporate earnings releases and the US Fed decision.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped over 700 points while Nifty 50 slipped below the key 22,400 mark in recent trading.
Bank Nifty tumbled nearly 3% to slip below the 55,000 mark.
IndiGo announced shifting 12 daily international departures to Navi Mumbai airport from February.
The government extended deadlines for companies to file their annual financial statements and returns.
summary: In the last trading session, Indian equity markets closed the week in deep red led by sharp selloffs and surging crude oil prices. Key benchmark indices dropped significantly as Bank Nifty slipped nearly 3% below 55,000 and Nifty fell below 22,400. Market participants are watching upcoming Q2 results, US Fed policy decisions, and crude oil movements for direction.
